## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Bhūripaññajātaka* (Ja 452) is a canonical birth story in the Jātaka collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Bearing the opening words "Is’t true, indeed", the traditional commentary or transmission notes that this tale—also designated as the *Bhūri-pañha* Birth—is given its full narrative exposition in the *Ummaggajātaka* (Ja 546) [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral connect the text at the passage level to four other major Jātakas: the *Mahāvāṇijajātaka* (Ja 493), the *Mahābodhijātaka* (Ja 528), the *Mūgapakkhajātaka* (Ja 538), and the *Vidhurajātaka* (Ja 546); it is also referenced in the Petavatthu (*Aṅkurapetavatthu*, Pv 21) [SuttaCentral]. Automatically computed text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates 48 matching Pali passages shared across eight works [DharmaNexus]. Substantial segments are shared with various volumes of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (most prominently with volume six, where §1.4–3.4 aligns with §2594–2598 at 0.93 similarity), the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the grammatical treatise *Saddanītippakaraṇaṃ* (*Dhātumālā*), and the *Maṇikuṇḍalajātaka* (Ja 351, sharing §8.4–10.4 with §4.1–5.4 at 1.0 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text tentatively with a Tibetan translation in the Kangyur, the *Nāgarājābherīgāthā* (D0325), across four passages [DharmaNexus].
None of the secondary literature passages matched in the search directly treat or analyze Ja 452; all instances represent false hits on the common Pali epithet *bhūripañña* ("one of vast wisdom"), found widely in devotional verses, other canonical suttas, and other Jātakas.
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
